'''Ravi D. Vakil''' (born February 22, 1970) is a Canadian-American mathematician working in [[algebraic geometry]]. He is the current president of the [[American Mathematical Society]].

==Education and career==
Vakil was born on February 22, 1970. His father was a professor of preventative medicine at the [[University of Toronto]] and his mother was a high school math teacher.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sfgate.com/education/article/STANFORD-Teacher-students-revel-in-joy-of-2465960.php |title=Teacher, students revel in joy of high-level math |author=Carrie Sturrock |date=December 2, 2006 |publisher=SFGATE }}
</ref> He later attended high school at [[Martingrove Collegiate Institute]] in [[Etobicoke]], Ontario, where he won several mathematical contests and olympiads.<ref>{{cite web|title=CMO Winners sorted by school by rank|url=http://cms.math.ca/Competitions/OMC/results/winschool|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|accessdate=August 18, 2016}}</ref> After earning a BSc and MSc from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1992, he completed a PhD in mathematics at [[Harvard University]] in 1997 under [[Joseph Daniel Harris|Joe Harris]].<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=18790 Mathematics genealogy]</ref>  He has since been an instructor at both [[Princeton University]] and [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]].  Since the fall of 2001, he has taught at [[Stanford University]],<ref>[http://math.stanford.edu/directory/faculty.html Stanford mathematics faculty]</ref> becoming a full professor in 2007. ''[[The Rising Sea: Foundations of Algebraic Geometry]]'', a mathematical textbook about algebraic geometry by Ravi Vakil, was published in 2025, although drafts were available online ever since he began to write it in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=Princeton University Press|url= https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691268668/the-rising-sea|accessdate=Jan 2, 2026}}</ref>

==Contributions==
Vakil is an [[algebraic geometry|algebraic geometer]] and his research work spans over [[enumerative geometry]], [[topology]], [[Gromov&ndash;Witten theory]], and classical algebraic geometry. He has solved several old problems in [[Schubert calculus]].  Among other results, he proved that all Schubert problems are enumerative<ref name="Schubert induction">{{cite journal | last=Vakil | first=Ravi | title=Schubert induction | journal=Annals of Mathematics | volume=164 | issue=2 | date=September 1, 2006 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2006.164.489 | pages=489–512| doi-access=free }}</ref> over the [[real number]]s, a result that resolves an issue mathematicians have worked on for at least two decades.

==Awards and honors==
Vakil has received many awards, including an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] CAREER Fellowship,  a [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|Sloan]] Research Fellowship, an [[American Mathematical Society]] Centennial Fellowship, a [[G. de B. Robinson Award|G. de B. Robinson prize]] for the best paper published (2000) in the [[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]] and the [[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]],<ref>[https://cms.math.ca/awards/g-de-b-robinson-award/ List of the G. de B. Robinson award's recipients], retrieved August 12, 2021.</ref> and the André-Aisenstadt Prize from the [[Centre de Recherches Mathématiques]] at the [[Université de Montréal]] (2005), and the [[Chauvenet Prize]]<ref name="ChauvenetVakil2014"/> (2014).

In 2013 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi |access-date=2025-03-30 |website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> Vakil was elected as its president in 2024 and began his two-year term on 1 February 2025.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Beebe |first1=Elaine |title=Interview with Ravi Vakil |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |date=January 2025 |volume=72 |issue=2 |page=214 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/202502/rnoti-p214.pdf |doi=10.1090/noti3113  |doi-access=free|access-date=5 February 2025}}</ref>

==Mathematics contests==
He was a member of the Canadian team in three [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]s, winning silver, gold (perfect score), and gold in 1986, 1987, and 1988 respectively. He was also the fourth person to be a four-time [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition|Putnam]] Fellow in the history of the contest.  Also, he has been the coordinator of weekly Putnam preparation seminars at Stanford.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/education/article/STANFORD-Teacher-students-revel-in-joy-of-2465960.php|title = STANFORD / Teacher, students revel in joy of high-level math|date = December 2, 2006}}</ref>
